errors.unauthorized: Not signed in or session expired.
errors.forbidden: Your role is not allowed to do this.
errors.step_up_required: This action requires confirming with your passkey again.
errors.token_invalid: The token is invalid, expired or already used.
errors.rate_limited: Too many attempts. Please wait a moment.
errors.lockout_protection: Refused because it would lock you out.
errors.helper_unavailable: The system service is not reachable.
errors.unavailable: This is not possible right now.
errors.csrf_failed: Security check failed. Please reload the page.
errors.passkey_cancelled: The passkey operation was cancelled or failed.
errors.webauthn_unsupported: This browser does not support passkeys.
errors.conflict: Conflict: the item already exists or was changed.
errors.permission_denied: Permission denied: your user's Linux permissions do not allow this.
errors.already_exists: An entry with this name already exists.
errors.symlink_refused: For security reasons symbolic links are not followed. Open the target directly.
errors.no_space: Not enough space on the disk.
errors.read_only_fs: The file system is mounted read-only.
errors.busy: The file is currently in use.
errors.path_blocked: This path belongs to Daemonica itself and is blocked in the file manager.
errors.sensitive_path: This is a sensitive file and needs an additional confirmation.
errors.protected_path: This path is protected and cannot be deleted, moved or renamed.
errors.virtual_fs: Files below /proc, /sys and /dev can only be viewed.
errors.limit_exceeded: The operation exceeds a limit (count, size or duration).
errors.not_supported: This is not supported on this system.
errors.not_regular_file: This is not a regular file.
errors.range_not_satisfiable: The requested range lies outside the file.
errors.mount_point: The operation would affect another mounted file system and was refused.
errors.root_mode_required: Root mode must be active for this.
errors.no_login_shell: This Linux user has no login shell.
errors.confirm_mismatch: The typed name does not match.

login.title: Sign in
login.intro: Sign in with your passkey – no password.
login.recovery: Lost your passkey? Recovery is only possible on the server: sudo daemonica-admin recover <account>

token.label: Setup token
token.help: Create the token on the server with: sudo daemonica-admin bootstrap
token.explain: The token proves you have access to the server. It is valid for 60 minutes and is consumed when the first passkey is registered.

domain.label: Dashboard domain
domain.help: The domain's DNS record must point to this server.
domain.explain: Passkeys are bound to the domain. That is why the first passkey is registered on the final domain.

allowlist.label: Allowed networks (one address or CIDR per line)
allowlist.help: Only connections from these networks are accepted – before the TLS handshake.
allowlist.publicWarning: Public means anyone on the Internet can see and attack the login page. Fixed networks, a VPN or an SSH tunnel are recommended.
allowlist.publicConfirm: I understand the risk and want to make the dashboard publicly reachable.
allowlist.explain: The default is “allowed networks only”. Local access (127.0.0.1, ::1) always remains allowed.

certificate.acmeHelp: Free, automatically issued certificate. Port 80 must briefly be free and reachable from the Internet.
certificate.staging: Let’s Encrypt Staging (testing only, not trusted by browsers)
certificate.tos: I accept the Let’s Encrypt terms of service.
certificate.working: Issuing certificate … this can take up to a minute.
certificate.explain: The dashboard only speaks TLS 1.3. The certificate is stored only for the web service.

switch.title: Switching to the final address
switch.text: The service restarts now and will be reachable at {{url}}. Open that address and enter the token again to register your first passkey.

passkey.linuxUserHelp: File access and the terminal run with this user's permissions. root is not allowed.
passkey.noUsers: There is no regular Linux user on the server. Create one first: sudo adduser <name>
passkey.name: Passkey name (e.g. laptop)
passkey.explain: Your device creates a key pair. The private key never leaves your device; the server stores only the public key.

done.title: All set!
done.text: The dashboard is set up and you are signed in. Register a second passkey next so you cannot lock yourself out.

recovery.title: Recover access
recovery.intro: Enter the token from “sudo daemonica-admin recover” and register a new passkey.

stepup.title: Confirm with passkey
stepup.text: This action is security-relevant. Confirm it with your passkey. The confirmation is valid for 5 minutes.

overview.title: Overview
overview.rebootRequired: A restart is required to complete updates.
overview.certExpiring_one: The dashboard certificate expires in {{count}} day.
overview.certExpiring_other: The dashboard certificate expires in {{count}} days.

passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.intro: Passkeys are your only sign-in method. Register at least two, e.g. laptop and phone.
passkeys.secondHint: Register a second passkey – without it, only server-side recovery helps if you lose this one.
passkeys.lastOne: The last passkey cannot be removed.

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.intro: See where you are signed in and end sessions. Sessions end automatically after 30 minutes of inactivity or at the latest after 12 hours.

invite.title: Accept invitation
invite.intro: An admin invited you to Daemonica. Register your passkey now – from then on you sign in with it only.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.intro: Dashboard accounts, their roles and mapped Linux users. Changes require passkey confirmation and end the affected account's sessions.
accounts.name: Name
accounts.inviteOnce: This link is shown only now and is valid once until {{time}}. Share it over a secure channel.
accounts.inviteExplain: Daemonica creates the account without a passkey and a one-time link (valid for 60 minutes). Whoever opens the link registers the first passkey for exactly this account. The token sits in the link fragment (#), so it is not sent to the server or logged until it is redeemed. The account acts with the rights of the chosen Linux user; root can never be mapped.
accounts.confirmRole: Change the role of “{{name}}”? All sessions of this account will be ended.
accounts.confirmDelete: Type “{{name}}” to delete. Passkeys and sessions are removed; the Linux user is left unchanged.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.intro: All security-relevant events, tamper-evident through a SHA-256 hash chain. Newest first.

settings.title: Settings
settings.intro: Access and behaviour of the dashboard. Risky changes are first shown as a plan, then applied and must be confirmed within 90 seconds – otherwise the server reverts them automatically.
settings.publicWarn: The dashboard is publicly reachable. Restricting it to known networks or a VPN is recommended.
settings.newListHelp: One entry per line as IP or CIDR, e.g. 203.0.113.5/32 or 2001:db8::/48. Loopback is always allowed.
settings.lockoutAck: I understand: my current IP {{ip}} will no longer be allowed. Without a confirmation from an allowed network the change is reverted after 90 seconds.
settings.publicAck: I deliberately want to make the dashboard publicly reachable.
settings.confirmPrompt: The new allowlist is active. Confirm within {{seconds}} s that you can still reach the dashboard; otherwise it is reverted automatically.
settings.rolledBackTimeout: No confirmation received – the server restored the previous allowlist.

risk.medium: Medium risk: networks that are removed lose access immediately.
risk.high: High risk: your own connection will be locked out.

settings.explain: Daemonica checks the allowlist when a connection is accepted, before TLS, and again on every request. After applying, the server closes your connection; the confirmation must arrive over a new connection and thereby proves you still get in with the new allowlist. The revert timer runs in the privileged helper – independent of the browser and the web process.
settings.moreLater: More settings (switch certificate, session lifetime, language) will follow.

services.title: Services
services.intro: systemd units on this server. Click a name for status, journal, unit file and dependencies.
services.protectedWarning: {{unit}} is a protected system service. Changing it may interrupt SSH or the dashboard. Continue? (You will confirm with your passkey.)
services.protectedHint: Protected service: changes for admins only, after passkey confirmation.
services.selfText: The dashboard will no longer be reachable. You can only start it again via SSH: sudo systemctl start daemonica-web

logs.title: Logs
logs.intro: System journal (journald). Filter by service, priority and time; search runs on the server.
logs.truncated: Result truncated – narrow the search or increase the line count.

processes.title: Processes
processes.intro: Running processes, refreshed every 3 seconds. Protected processes (e.g. PID 1, SSH, Daemonica) cannot be signalled.
processes.truncated: List truncated (too many processes) – the busiest are shown.

sig.KILL: Kill immediately – unsaved data is lost

users.title: Users
users.intro: Linux users and groups on this server. Changes require admin rights and a passkey confirmation.
users.advanced: Advanced: show and change system users
users.name: Name
users.grantSudoConfirm: {{name}} will get full administrator rights (root via sudo). Continue?
users.revokeSudoConfirm: {{name}} will lose administrator rights via sudo. Continue?
users.created: User {{name}} created. Add an SSH key next.
users.adminMappedWarning: {{name}} is mapped to an active dashboard admin. This change can lock you out of the dashboard. Really continue?
users.nameHelp: Lower-case letters, digits, - and _; starts with a letter or _.
users.createExplain: The user is created without a password (login locked). Add an SSH key next – key pairs are created on your computer with ssh-keygen -t ed25519.
users.passwordHint: SSH keys are safer for logging in. A password is needed e.g. for sudo.
users.deleteWarning: The user is deleted permanently. Running processes of the user must be stopped first.

sshkeys.title: SSH keys
sshkeys.intro: Public keys allowed to log in as a user via SSH (authorized_keys). Create key pairs on your computer with: ssh-keygen -t ed25519
sshkeys.readOnly: The authorized_keys file is outside the home directory or a symbolic link – it is shown read-only.
sshkeys.problems: File permissions are unsafe – sshd may ignore the keys:

problem.owner: {{path}} is not owned by the user
problem.mode: {{path}} is readable or writable by others

sshkeys.confirmRemove: Remove key “{{name}}”? Logins with this key will no longer work.
sshkeys.publicKeyHelp: Paste the content of the .pub file. Allowed: Ed25519, ECDSA, security keys (sk-…), RSA with at least 3072 bits.
sshkeys.commandWarning: With command= the key can only run this one command. A mistake here can make the access unusable.
sshkeys.explain: The key is written to the user's authorized_keys with the user's own permissions (atomically, mode 0600).
sshkeys.hostKeysHelp: Compare these fingerprints with what your SSH client shows on first connect.
sshkeys.sshdReadOnly: Read-only (sshd -T). Changes follow via the security checklist in phase 2.

files.title: Files
files.intro: Files and folders of this server. You work as Linux user {{user}} – its permissions apply.
files.introRoot: Root mode active: you work as root. Every change is recorded in the audit log.
files.readonly: The file manager is not available to the read-only role.
files.notWritable: You have no write permission in this folder.
files.notWritableAdmin: You have no write permission in this folder. As an admin you can enable root mode.
files.rootHint: As an admin you can enable root mode to read here.
files.truncated: This folder contains very many entries; only the first 100,000 are considered.
files.virtual: This is a kernel pseudo file system: contents can be viewed but not changed or downloaded.
files.empty: This folder is empty. Create a file or drop files here to upload them.
files.dropHint: Tip: drop files onto the list to upload them (max. {{limit}} MiB per file).
files.rawName: This name contains invalid characters. Rename the entry to open it.
files.name: Name
files.invalidName: Invalid name: no “/”, no control characters, not “.” or “..”.
files.invalidPath: Please enter an absolute path, e.g. /home/alice.
files.destinationHelp: Absolute path of an existing folder. Existing entries are never overwritten.
files.moveExplain: Within one file system a move is a quick rename. Between disks the data is copied and the original deleted afterwards.

perm.specialWarning: Setuid/setgid make programs run with the owner's or group's rights. Only set them if you know exactly why.

files.chownExplain: Only root can change owners. The change is recorded in the audit log. Empty fields stay unchanged.

props.sensitive: Sensitive file: reading or changing it needs a warning confirmation and your passkey.

files.deleteWarning: The file is deleted permanently. There is no recycle bin.
files.deleteDirWarning: The folder is deleted permanently. A non-empty folder is only removed with “Delete contents”.
files.deleteLink: Only the link is deleted, not its target.

upload.title: Uploads
upload.noFolders: Folders cannot be uploaded – only individual files.

root.title: Enable root mode
root.warning: In root mode Linux permissions no longer apply: you can read and change system files. A mistake can render the server unusable.
root.explain: Root mode applies to this session only and ends automatically after 10 minutes. It requires a confirmation with your passkey. Daemonica's own data stays blocked even as root; every change is recorded.
root.bar: ROOT MODE in the file manager – ends in {{time}}

sensitive.title: Sensitive file
sensitive.text: This file contains especially sensitive data (e.g. password hashes or private keys). Only open or change it if really necessary.
sensitive.stepUp: For security you will be asked for your passkey next. The access is recorded.

editor.savedInPlace: Saved (written into the existing file so that owner and links are kept).
editor.readOnly: Read-only: the file belongs to {{owner}} and your user may not change it.
editor.readOnlyAdmin: Read-only: the file belongs to {{owner}}. As an admin you can edit it in root mode.
editor.binary: This is not a text file (binary data or not UTF-8 encoded) and is not opened in the editor.
editor.tooLarge: The file is larger than 5 MiB and is not opened in the editor.
editor.label: Contents of {{name}}
editor.keys: Ctrl+S save · Ctrl+F find · Esc, then Tab leaves the editor
editor.conflictText: Someone changed the file since you opened it (last at {{time}}, owner {{user}}). Review the differences.
editor.diffLegend: Red: only on the server · Green: only in your version
editor.diffTooLarge: The files are too large to compare.
editor.leaveText: Your changes are not saved yet. Leave anyway?
editor.savedDespite: Saved although the check with {{tool}} failed. The service may not accept the faulty settings.
editor.checkBlocked: {{tool}} found errors. The file was not saved, because a broken sudo configuration can lock out all root access.
editor.checkRolledBack: {{tool}} found errors. The change was undone right away; the file has its previous content again. Your changes are still in the editor.
editor.checkNotSaved: {{tool}} found errors. The file was not saved.
editor.versionsText: Before a file below /etc is saved, its old content is kept (30 days, at most 20 versions).
editor.versionsOff: No versions are kept for this file.
editor.versionOf: Version from {{time}} compared with the editor.
editor.versionLegend: Red: only in the editor · Green: only in the version
editor.versionSame: The version is identical to the editor content.
editor.versionLoaded: Version from {{time}} loaded. Save to restore it.
editor.savedPreexisting: Saved. The check with {{tool}} fails, but it already failed before this change. Review the configuration before reloading the service.

table.numberHelp: Number (at least), >, >=, <, <=, = or a range a-b. Sizes with K, M, G, T (e.g. <500K, 1M-2G).

terminal.title: Terminal
terminal.intro: Shell on this server as Linux user {{user}}.
terminal.readonly: The terminal is not available with the read-only role.
terminal.newHint: Shell as your Linux user (without sudo)
terminal.rootHint: Shell as root – asks for your passkey every time, ends after 30 minutes
terminal.sudoHint: Shell as your Linux user with sudo per sudoers – asks for your passkey every time, ends after 30 minutes
terminal.full: {{max}} terminals are already open. Close one to open another.
terminal.bar_one: ELEVATED: a terminal with elevated rights is open – ends in {{time}}
terminal.bar_other: ELEVATED: {{count}} terminals with elevated rights are open – the first ends in {{time}}

ended.expired: The 30 minutes of elevated rights are over.
ended.session_ended: Your sign-in has ended or changed.
ended.allowlist: Your address is no longer in the allowlist.

note.standard: In this terminal sudo, su and setuid programs have no effect.
note.sudo: sudo works here as sudoers allows – {{user}} needs an entry there (e.g. member of group sudo).

change.keep: I am still connected – keep it

network.title: Network
network.intro: Interfaces, routes, DNS and open ports of this server. Changes go through preview → apply → confirm and are reverted automatically after 90 seconds without confirmation.

readOnly.mixed: Several systems configure the network on this server at the same time. Daemonica only shows the configuration so they do not overwrite each other.
readOnly.not_implemented: Daemonica only shows this network manager so far. Change it with its own tools (e.g. nmcli) in the terminal.
readOnly.unsupported: No supported network manager detected – the configuration is shown only.

network.sessionHint: Your current dashboard connection runs over this interface.
network.portsIntro: Listening TCP ports and open UDP ports with their process – the same list as “ss -tulnp”.

notEditable.several_files: This interface is configured in several files ({{file}}). To lose nothing, Daemonica only shows it.
notEditable.advanced: This interface uses settings Daemonica does not edit (e.g. bridge, bond or routing options). It is shown only.
notEditable.manager: The network manager of this server is shown only.

network.sessionWarn: Your current connection (from {{ip}}) runs over {{name}}. A wrong setting disconnects you – without confirmation the server reverts after 90 seconds.
network.addressesHelp: One address per line with prefix length, e.g. 192.0.2.10/24 or 2001:db8::10/64.
network.lockoutAck: I understand that I am changing the interface of my own connection ({{name}}) and may have to open the dashboard at a new address afterwards.
network.explain: Daemonica checks the configuration with the network manager's tool before applying it. After applying you have 90 seconds to confirm over a new connection. If that fails, the server restores the previous configuration by itself.
network.confirmPrompt: The new network configuration is active. Confirm within {{seconds}} s that you can still reach the dashboard; otherwise the server reverts automatically.

risk.medium: Medium risk: connections over this interface may be interrupted briefly.
risk.high: Red alert: this interface carries your own connection. A mistake disconnects you until the server reverts after 90 seconds.

network.rolledBackTimeout: No confirmation received – the server restored the previous network configuration.
network.newUrl: Your address changes. Confirm at the new address:

firewall.title: Firewall
firewall.intro: Status, rules and reachability of the host firewall. Changes go through preview, apply and confirm; without confirmation the server reverts after 90 seconds.

light.green: Green: firewall active, nothing to report
light.red: Red: the server is not protected

hint.inactive: The firewall is off. Every listening service is reachable from outside.
hint.default_allow: The default policy for incoming connections is “allow”: anything no rule forbids gets through.
hint.not_persistent: The firewall runs but will not start again after a reboot.
hint.ipv6_off: IPv6 is off in ufw, but the server has a public IPv6 address. IPv6 connections are not filtered.
hint.logging_off: Logging is off. Blocked connections do not show up in the firewall logs.
hint.unused_allow: A rule allows {{arg}}, but no service listens there (any more). The rule can probably go.
hint.readonly: The firewall ({{arg}}) is not managed by Daemonica and is read-only.

firewall.allGood: Incoming connections are blocked by default; only the rules below let traffic in.
firewall.loggingHelp: “Low” logs blocked packets (rate-limited). Higher levels also log allowed connections and produce a lot of log volume.
firewall.rulesIntro: ufw checks the rules top to bottom; the first matching rule decides.
firewall.noUfwRules: No rule set Daemonica can manage. The raw view shows the active rules.

actionHelp.limit: Allows, but blocks sources with more than 6 connections in 30 seconds (protects against password guessing).
actionHelp.deny: Silently drops packets; the sender waits for a timeout.
actionHelp.reject: Refuses at once; the sender learns that the port is closed.

firewall.noneInfo: No firewall is active on this server. Daemonica manages ufw and can set it up.
firewall.readonlyInfo: This firewall ({{backend}}) is not managed by Daemonica. Status and raw view are readable; make changes with this firewall's own tools.
firewall.installExplain: Installs the ufw package with safe defaults (deny incoming, allow outgoing). The firewall stays off; when you enable it, Daemonica proposes rules for SSH and the dashboard.
firewall.installed: ufw is installed. Review the proposed rules, then enable the firewall.
firewall.reachIntro: Listening services and what the firewall does with a new connection from the internet. “Unprotected” means no rule covers the port and the connection still gets through.

lockout.dashboard: Your dashboard connection (TCP {{port}}) would be blocked.
lockout.ssh: SSH (TCP {{port}}) would no longer be reachable from your IP.
lockout.ssh_closed: SSH (TCP {{port}}) would no longer be reachable from the internet.

firewall.lockoutAck: I have a second way in (the provider's console) and know I can lock myself out from {{ip}}. Without confirmation the server reverts after 90 seconds.
firewall.enableExplain: When enabling, Daemonica adds rules where needed that keep SSH (port {{ports}}) and the dashboard (port {{port}}, for the allowlist networks) reachable. You see them in the preview and must accept them.
firewall.disableWarn: Without a firewall every listening service is reachable from the internet.
firewall.resetWarn: Reset deletes all rules, restores the default policies and turns the firewall off. ufw keeps the previous files with a timestamp.
firewall.typeName: Type the server name “{{name}}” to confirm
firewall.autoTitle: These rules are added before enabling so you are not locked out:
firewall.autoAck: I reviewed the rules and accept them.
firewall.portHelp: e.g. 22, 80,443 or 6000:6010 (lists and ranges need TCP or UDP).
firewall.addrHelp: “any” or an IP address or network (CIDR).
firewall.commentHelp: Optional, max. 80 characters. Comments starting with “daemonica:” mark rules Daemonica manages.
firewall.confirmPrompt: The new firewall configuration is active. Confirm within {{seconds}} s that you still reach the dashboard; otherwise the server reverts automatically.

risk.medium: Medium risk: check that the preview matches your intent.
risk.high: Red alert: this change can cut your own connection. Without confirmation the server reverts after 90 seconds.

firewall.rolledBackTimeout: No confirmation received – the server restored the previous firewall configuration.

logs.intro: Firewall events logged by the kernel, read from journald. All fields are validated on the server; there are no external lookups (GeoIP, reverse DNS).
logs.off: Firewall logging is off, so no entries appear here. The recommended level is “low”: it logs blocked connections with rate limiting. Note: IP addresses are personal data.
logs.highWarn: Logging is set to “high” or “full”: allowed connections are logged as well. This produces a lot of journal volume and stores more personal data.
logs.truncated: result truncated, narrow the time range or filters
logs.empty: No firewall entries in this time range.

firewall.prependHelp: Needed so a block also hits ports that a later rule allows (ufw prepend).

capture.title: Packet capture
capture.intro: Capture the traffic of one interface for a limited time, watch a live summary and download it as .pcap for Wireshark. Headers only, unless you choose full packets under “Advanced”.
capture.adminOnly: Packet captures are available to admins only.
capture.missing: tcpdump is not installed. Captures need tcpdump.
capture.retentionSaved: Retention saved. Older captures were deleted.
capture.deleteAllConfirm_one: Permanently delete {{count}} capture? A running capture is kept.
capture.deleteAllConfirm_other: Permanently delete {{count}} captures? A running capture is kept.

warning.title: Privacy and authorisation
warning.text: Captures can contain confidential and personal data, and with unencrypted protocols also credentials and contents. Only capture traffic you are authorised to capture. Start and download are recorded in the audit log (without contents).
warning.ack: I have read the notice and I am authorised to make this capture.

host.name: Connection problem with a host
host.help: All traffic from and to one address.

custom.name: Custom filter
custom.help: Build the filter yourself or enter a BPF expression under “Advanced”.

capture.hostHelp: IPv4 or IPv6 address, optionally with a prefix (e.g. 10.0.0.0/8).
capture.hostBad: Not a valid address or network.
capture.portsHelp: Up to 10 ports, separated by commas or spaces.
capture.portsBad: Ports must be numbers from 1 to 65535 (at most 10).
capture.portsNoProto: ICMP and ARP have no ports.
capture.advancedHelp: Free BPF expression and full packets.
capture.exprHelp: As for tcpdump, e.g. “tcp port 443 and not net 10.0.0.0/8”. Allowed are letters, digits, spaces and . : / ( ) [ ] ! & | = < > + * -, no leading “-”. The expression is checked before the start.
capture.exprBad: The expression contains characters that are not allowed or starts with “-”.
capture.includeDashHelp: By default TCP port {{port}} is excluded so that the live view does not capture itself.
capture.limitsBad: Please check the limits: duration 1 to 30 minutes, size 1 to 1024 MiB.
capture.promiscHelp: Also accept packets not addressed to this server. Rarely needed.
capture.fullHelp: Store whole packets instead of only the first 96 bytes (headers).
capture.fullWarning: Full packets include the payload. With unencrypted protocols that means e.g. passwords, e-mails and file contents. The file then needs particular protection.
capture.fullAck: I deliberately want to capture the payload.
capture.snaplenNote: Only the first 96 bytes of each packet are stored (headers). Full packets are under “Advanced”.
capture.explain: On start you confirm with your passkey. Daemonica checks the filter with tcpdump, then runs tcpdump as its own strongly restricted service without root rights (packet receive only, no write access) and writes the file itself. The capture ends at the first limit reached or when free disk space drops below 10 %. It is deleted automatically when the retention period ends.

jobs.title: Tasks and jobs
jobs.intro: Scheduled tasks on this server: your own jobs as systemd timers, every existing timer and cron.
jobs.managedIntro: Jobs created by Daemonica (systemd service and timer daemonica-job-…).
jobs.timersIntro: Every timer systemd knows, with its next and last run.
jobs.cronIntro: Entries from /etc/crontab, /etc/cron.d, the cron.* folders and user crontabs.
jobs.empty: No jobs yet. Create the first one with “New job”.
jobs.driftHelp: The unit files were changed outside Daemonica or are missing. Saving the job overwrites them.
jobs.deleteConfirm: Delete job {{id}} with its service and timer? Its history in the journal stays.

harden.safeHelp: No privilege escalation, private /tmp, system read-only except the allowed paths, kernel and devices protected.
harden.noneHelp: The job may do anything its user may do. Only choose this when hardening prevents the job from working.

jobs.nextApprox: Next runs (counted from when the timer is enabled)
jobs.noRuns: No runs in the journal yet.
jobs.descriptionHelp: What does the job do? Shown in the list and the journal.
jobs.idHelp: Lower-case letters, digits and dashes. The unit becomes {{unit}}.
jobs.userHelp: The command runs as this Linux user.
jobs.rootWarning: Runs as root: the command has full rights on the server. Saving asks for a passkey confirmation.

exec.name: Program
exec.help: A program with arguments, no shell. Recommended.

script.name: Script
script.help: A script file, run directly or through an interpreter.

shell.name: Shell command (advanced)
shell.help: One line for /bin/sh with pipes and variables.

jobs.scriptHelp: Absolute path of the script file.
jobs.argsHelp: Separated by spaces, with "…" around arguments that contain spaces. No shell interprets any of it.
jobs.shellWarning: Shell commands are interpreted by /bin/sh: variables, $( … ), ; and | take effect. Only use this when a program with arguments is not enough, and never build in input from others.
jobs.shellAck: I understand that a shell interprets this command.
jobs.calendarHelp: Syntax as OnCalendar= in systemd.time, e.g. Mon..Fri *-*-* 07:30.
jobs.shortMonths: Months without this day are skipped.
jobs.timezoneHelp: Leave empty for the server's time zone.
jobs.randomDelayHelp: Spreads the start so that jobs do not all start at once.
jobs.persistentHelp: If the server was off at the scheduled time, the job runs after boot.

describe.monthly: On day {{day}} of every month at {{time}}

jobs.timeoutHelp: The run is stopped after this. Default 60 minutes.
jobs.envHelp: Values are stored in the unit file, which everyone on the server can read. Do not put passwords here.
jobs.writePathsHelp: One path per line. Everything else is read-only for the job.
jobs.noHardeningWarning: Without hardening the job can change anything its user can change.
jobs.checkFirst: The server checks the job before it is saved.
jobs.serverRejected: The server rejected a value. The field is marked.
jobs.explain: Daemonica writes a systemd service and a timer to /etc/systemd/system, reloads systemd and enables the timer. Every value is escaped for systemd, so special characters cannot add settings. Output goes to the journal.

warn.short_months: Months with fewer days are skipped.

err.id: Only lower-case letters, digits and dashes, at most 48 characters.
err.description: No line breaks or backslashes, at most 200 characters.
err.args: Close the quotes, no line breaks.
err.path: Absolute path without spaces or special characters.
err.env: Names of letters, digits and _, each once, no control characters.
err.missing: Does not exist or is not a regular file.
err.untrusted: The file or a folder belongs to another user or is writable by others. Someone could replace the command.
err.rejected: systemd does not accept this schedule.

jobs.cronMissing: cron is not installed. systemd timers work regardless.
jobs.cronDeleteConfirm: Delete this entry from the crontab of {{user}}?
jobs.cronScheduleHelp: minute hour day month weekday, e.g. 0 3 * * * for daily at 3 am.
jobs.cronShell: cron runs the command through /bin/sh. A % is stored as a plain character.
jobs.fromLibraryHelp: Sets the path and, for files that are not executable, a matching interpreter.
jobs.cronServerTime: The time applies in the server's time zone ({{tz}}). cron does not catch up on missed runs.
jobs.tzLocalServer: Times in your local time ({{local}}). The server runs on {{server}}.

scripts.intro: Your own scripts and script collections from GitHub, stored under {{root}}. Jobs and terminals use them by this path.
scripts.empty: No scripts yet. Write one or add a collection from GitHub.
scripts.removeConfirm: The collection {{id}} and all its files under {{dir}} will be deleted.
scripts.tooLarge: The file is too large to show (over 128 KiB).
scripts.name: File name
scripts.nameHelp: Letters, digits and . _ - @ +, no spaces, not starting with a dot.
scripts.execLabel: Executable (runs directly, needs a shebang line)
scripts.rootNote: Root jobs can run scripts from the library. That is why every change needs your passkey and is written to the audit log.

err.name: Invalid file name.
err.taken: A local script with this name exists.
err.size: The script is larger than 128 KiB.
err.repo: Use the form owner/repository or a github.com link.
err.token: The token must not contain spaces.
err.id: Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, at most 40 characters, not “local”.

fetch.not_found: Repository, branch or commit not found. Private repositories need a token.
fetch.unauthorized: GitHub refused access. Check the token and its permissions (Contents: read).
fetch.rate_limited: GitHub rate limit reached. Try again later or use a token.
fetch.too_large: The collection is too large (at most 2000 files, 32 MiB, 1 MiB per file). Choose a subfolder.
fetch.network: GitHub cannot be reached right now.

scripts.addIntro: Daemonica downloads the repository at a fixed commit. You see all files first and confirm with your passkey. Later changes in the repository only arrive when you check for an update and accept it.
scripts.refHelp: Leave empty for the default branch. A full commit hash pins for good.
scripts.subdirHelp: Only take files from this folder (empty: the whole repository).
scripts.tokenHelp: Only for private repositories: a fine-grained token with read access to contents. It stays on the server and is never shown again.
scripts.sourceIdHelp: Becomes part of the path the files are stored under.
scripts.upToDate: The collection is up to date.
scripts.usedChanged: These changes affect files that jobs use: {{files}}
scripts.reviewNote: Review the changes. Exactly this commit is installed, even if the branch has moved on since.
scripts.diffOmitted: The diff is too large to show. Look at it on GitHub.

skip.name: name with spaces or special characters

updates.title: Updates and packages
updates.intro: Install updates, set up automatic security updates and manage packages.
updates.refreshListsHint: Runs apt update and downloads the current package lists of all sources.
updates.locked: Package management is locked by {{comm}} (PID {{pid}}, {{file}}). A new job waits up to 10 minutes for the lock.
updates.rebootRequired: A reboot is required for all updates to take effect.
updates.needRestart_one: {{count}} service still uses old libraries and should be restarted:
updates.needRestart_other: {{count}} services still use old libraries and should be restarted:
updates.noNeedrestart: needrestart is not installed, so there is no hint about services to restart.

phase.lock: Waiting for the package management lock

state.unknown: Result unknown (interrupted, e.g. by a reboot)

updates.conffiles: These configuration files were kept although the package ships a new version. The new version is next to it as .dpkg-dist, please compare:
updates.kept: Kept back (need a decision, e.g. new dependencies or removals): {{pkgs}}
updates.ackExtra_one: I checked that the additional package may be removed.
updates.ackExtra_other: I checked that the {{count}} additional packages may be removed.
updates.critical: Critical: {{pkgs}}. Without these packages the server may become unreachable or unusable.
updates.explainJob: Daemonica simulated the job with apt-get -s. On start it simulates again; if the plan changed, nothing runs. The job runs on as its own systemd unit even if you close the page. Changed configuration files are kept.
updates.updateExplain: Downloads the current package lists of all sources (apt update). The list then shows the new updates.
updates.dryRunExplain: Runs unattended-upgrade --dry-run --debug: shows which packages would be installed automatically, without changing anything.

auto.setupIntro: Installs only security updates from the distribution's official sources, daily.
auto.rebootHelp: Only when an update requires a reboot, at the chosen time (server time).
auto.timeInvalid: Please enter a time as HH:MM.
auto.explain: Daemonica writes /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/52daemonica-unattended-upgrades. It is read after the distribution's defaults and replaces their origin list with the security origins. The dry run shows what unattended-upgrades would do.
auto.unsupported: This distribution is not supported for the setup (Debian and Ubuntu only).

updates.termInvalid: Please enter a single word of letters, digits, dot, plus, minus or underscore (2 to 64 characters).
updates.moreResults: There are more results than shown. Please narrow the search.
updates.sourcesIntro: Package sources are shown only. Unofficial sources are marked.

err.package_job_running: A package job is already running. Please wait until it has finished.
err.plan_changed: The plan changed since the simulation. Please review the new simulation.
err.critical_unconfirmed: Removing critical packages must be confirmed.
err.protected_package: Daemonica itself cannot be removed through Daemonica.
err.simulation_failed: The simulation failed; nothing was changed.

disks.title: Disks and mounts
disks.intro: Block devices, usage, mounting and unmounting and the file /etc/fstab. Partitioning and formatting are not part of it.
disks.lsblkFailed: The device list could not be read (lsblk).
disks.devicesIntro: All block devices with partitions. A device with a file system can be added to fstab from its menu.
disks.unmountConfirm: {{target}} will be unmounted. Programs using files there lose access. If the mount is busy, Daemonica shows the processes and unmounts nothing.
disks.busy: {{target}} is busy and was not unmounted.

err.protected_mount: This mount belongs to the system and cannot be unmounted through Daemonica.

problem.prefer_uuid: Better use UUID= instead of a device name; device names can change on reboot.
problem.nofail_recommended: Recommended: set nofail so a missing disk does not block the boot.
problem.root_missing: The entry for / must not be removed.

disks.unsaved: Unsaved changes. Saving checks the file and applies it with a confirmation timer.
disks.fstabIntro: Entries of /etc/fstab. Changes are saved only after a check.
disks.rejected: The fstab is faulty and was not saved. Please fix the marked points.
disks.fstabExplain: Daemonica checks the new file itself and then with findmnt --verify. Only when both pass is it saved: first a backup /etc/fstab.daemonica-<time> is made, then systemd reloads the mount units. If you do not confirm within 90 seconds, the server restores the old file. Saving mounts or unmounts nothing.
disks.confirmPrompt: The new fstab is active. Please confirm within {{seconds}} s, otherwise the old file is restored.

risk.medium: Medium risk: an error in fstab can hold up the next boot. The file was checked and a backup is made.

disks.rolledBackTimeout: No confirmation received – the server restored the previous fstab.
disks.fileInvalid: Please enter an absolute path (none for swap).
disks.specHelp: Prefer UUID=…; the list shows all devices with a file system.
disks.preferUuid: Device names like /dev/sdb1 can change. Better use UUID=.
disks.passHelp: 1 only for /, 2 for other file systems, 0 for no check.
disks.nofailHint: Without nofail a missing disk stops the boot.

timehost.title: Time & host
timehost.intro: Time zone, time synchronisation and host name of the server, plus reboot and power-off.
timehost.daemonsMissing: Not all system services answered: {{names}}. Their details are missing.
timehost.drift: The server clock differs from this browser's clock by {{s}} seconds.
timehost.localRtc: The hardware clock runs in local time. That causes trouble at daylight saving changes; UTC is usual.
timehost.ntpSwitch: Synchronise the time over the network (NTP)
timehost.timeExplain: The time zone is set by systemd-timedated (timedatectl set-timezone). It only changes how local time is shown, not the clock itself; logs and schedules such as cron follow it. Synchronisation switches the first available NTP service on or off, usually systemd-timesyncd.
timehost.hostnameHelp: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, at most 63 characters. The domain belongs into /etc/hosts or DNS.

hostnameProblem.dot: No dot or domain, just the short name.
hostnameProblem.invalid: Allowed are a–z, 0–9 and hyphens, not at the start or end.

timehost.updateHosts: Also change the name in /etc/hosts (recommended, otherwise sudo reports “unable to resolve host”)
timehost.cloudInit: cloud-init is active and may reset the host name at the next boot. Add “preserve_hostname: true” in /etc/cloud/cloud.cfg.d/ to make it permanent.
timehost.cloudInitHosts: cloud-init also manages /etc/hosts here (manage_etc_hosts) and rewrites it from /etc/cloud/templates/hosts.debian.tmpl at every boot, so the change to /etc/hosts only lasts until the next reboot.
timehost.hostExplain: Daemonica sets the name through systemd-hostnamed (like hostnamectl). /etc/hosts is updated first and backed up as /etc/hosts.daemonica-timestamp. If setting the name fails, /etc/hosts is written back. Open shells show the old name until the next login.
timehost.powerIntro: A reboot drops all connections. The page waits and reconnects once the server is back.
timehost.rebootExplain: All services stop; open terminals, transfers and package installs are cut off.
timehost.poweroffExplain: The server is switched off and can no longer be reached.
timehost.poweroffWarn: Daemonica cannot switch the server back on. Only your provider's panel can (Hostinger: hPanel → VPS → Start).
timehost.blocked: These programs currently want to prevent a shutdown: {{who}}. As administrator you can go ahead anyway; their work is cut off.
timehost.typeName: Type the host name “{{name}}” to confirm

err.confirm_mismatch: The typed name does not match the host name.

scheduledOk.reboot: Reboot scheduled for {{at}}. Logged-in users get a message.
scheduledOk.poweroff: Power-off scheduled for {{at}}. Logged-in users get a message.

offline.reboot: The server cannot be reached right now. The page reconnects as soon as it is back.
offline.poweroff: The server is off. Once you start it again in your provider's panel, the page reconnects by itself.

timeout.reboot: The server is not back after 10 minutes.

timeoutHint.reboot: Check your provider's panel (console, status). The page keeps trying.
timeoutHint.poweroff: Start it in your provider's panel. The page keeps trying.

reconnect.back: The server is back. The page reloads its data.
